newsitem.title: USA: U.S. plays down closure of Korea border office.
newsitem.headline: U.S. plays down closure of Korea border office.

text.p: The United States on Tuesday played down a decision by North Korea to temporarily abandon a border liaison office with South Korea, saying it had never fulfilled its intended role.

The office in the border hamlet of Panmunjom was set up to promote civilian contacts, including cultural and government exchanges, and to facilitate family reunions after North and South Korea signed a non-aggression treaty in 1991.

"The liaison office ... was unable to fulfil its intended function because there were not, and have not been up to this point, the expanded cross-border contacts that were spoken of in the 1991 agreement," a State Department spokesman said.
"It was an office that for the last five years didn't do much, if anything, and so closed down," said spokesman Glyn Davies.

The official (North) Korean Central News Agency said Pyongyang's action was in response to remarks by South Korean President Kim Young-sam that it said had shut the door to dialogue between the two countries.
The move was seen as indicating a further deterioration of relations that have turned icy following the incursion of a North Korean submarine into South Korean waters in September.
